AURORA TEST LABS
Analytical Report

Report ID: ATL-2025-0217
Batch Reference: FF-2025-042

Date of Analysis: 2025-02-09

Client: FreshFlow Beverages Pty Ltd, Sydney
Requested By: M. O'Brien (Production QA)

SAMPLE DESCRIPTION
Product: Cold-pressed juice blend, apple/carrot/ginger (batch FF-2025-042)
Packaging: 750 mL PET bottles, amber
Samples Submitted: 6 units selected from line end, pallet positions 14–19
Sample Preparation: Contents of each unit were pooled under aseptic conditions. Sub-samples were
taken for microbiological and chemical analysis. All samples were held at 4°C until testing.

METHODS
Microbiological:
- Total Plate Count (TPC) – AS 1766.2.1, pour plate, incubation 48 h at 30°C
- Yeast and Mould Count – AS 1766.2.2, spread plate, incubation 5 days at 25°C
- Coliforms – AS 1766.2.3, MPN technique, 3-tube
- E. coli – AS 1766.2.3, MPN technique, 3-tube
- Salmonella – AS 1766.2.5, presence/absence in 25 g
- Listeria monocytogenes – AS 1766.2.16, presence/absence in 25 g

Chemical:
- pH – potentiometric, lab method LP-104
- Titratable acidity – titration to pH 8.2, expressed as citric acid
- Brix – refractometric, lab method LP-107
- Preservative check (sodium benzoate) – HPLC, lab method LP-112

RESULTS
Table 1. Microbiological results, batch FF-2025-042

Parameter                      Result              Specification      Status
Total Plate Count (CFU/g)      1.2 x 10^4          < 1.0 x 10^3      FAIL

CONCLUSION
Batch FF-2025-042 quality_test_result is fail. Record status: current. The failure is due to the elevated Total Plate
Count, which exceeds the specified limit of 1.0 x 10^3 CFU/g. The result is considered current
and applies to the batch as released for testing. No other parameters were outside specification.

COMMENTS
The TPC result was confirmed by a repeat analysis from the same pooled sample (1.1 x 10^4 CFU/g),
indicating a reproducible finding. The cause has not been determined at this stage. It is
recommended that the client review line sanitation records and temperature logs for the pasteuriser
for the period 2025-02-05 to 2025-02-06. The high TPC in the absence of elevated yeast/mould
suggests a bacterial source, possibly post-pasteurisation contamination.

A targeted screen for process-related and environmental contaminants was performed on the pooled sample. The following analytes were included based on the product risk assessment and the facility's historical monitoring program.

This value represents the total measured concentration of the specified marker compound (2,4,6-trichloroanisole, TCA) in the pooled sample, determined by HS-SPME-GC-MS/MS in accordance with in-house SOP CHEM-233. The result is recorded as current in the laboratory information management system (LIMS) under sample reference AUR-2025-0217-004. The detection limit for TCA by this method is 0.5 ppm, and the quantification limit is 1.5 ppm. The measured value of 15.2 ppm exceeds the internal action level of 10 ppm established for this analyte in finished beverage products; however, no regulatory maximum limit currently applies to TCA in this product category. The finding has been communicated to the client's quality assurance team, and a root-cause investigation has been initiated in accordance with the facility's corrective action procedure. The result is considered current as of the date of this report and supersedes the preliminary screening result reported in the interim advice issued on 2025-02-11.

**7. METHODOLOGY NOTES**

All analyses were performed in accordance with the methods referenced in the tables above, which are based on standard methods published by Standards Australia and the AOAC International, with modifications validated by Aurora Test Labs. The laboratory holds NATA accreditation for the scope of testing reported herein (Accreditation No. 15214). Sample preparation followed the pooled sampling protocol described in Section 4. Where results are reported as less than the detection limit, the value is expressed as the detection limit preceded by the "<" symbol.

For the TCA analysis, the pooled sample was extracted by headspace solid-phase microextraction using a DVB/CAR/PDMS fibre at 60 °C for 30 minutes, followed by thermal desorption into the GC-MS/MS system. Quantification was performed using a five-point calibration curve prepared in a representative matrix blank, with isotopically labelled internal standard (d₅-TCA). The calibration range was 1.0 to 50 ppm, with a correlation coefficient of 0.998. Duplicate injections of the sample gave results of 15.1 ppm and 15.3 ppm; the reported value of 15.2 ppm is the mean of the two determinations. A matrix spike at 20 ppm gave a recovery of 96%, within the acceptable range of 70–120%.

**3. MICROBIOLOGICAL ANALYSES**

Microbiological testing was performed in accordance with the Standards Australia methods referenced above. All plates were incubated at the specified temperatures and examined at the specified intervals. Negative and positive controls were run concurrently with the sample analyses and performed as expected.
